title: The Biggest Plus Sign That Fits Between the Blocked Cells

concept.title: For every cell, count the free cells in a row in each of the four directions, and take the smallest
body: An `n` by `n` grid has some **blocked cells**, and all the other cells are free. A *plus sign of order `k`* has a free centre and four arms (up, down, left, right), each with `k - 1` free cells next to the centre (so it has `4(k - 1) + 1` cells, all free). Find the largest order of a plus sign in the grid, or 0 if every cell is blocked. For a free 5 by 5 grid with only the centre blocked, the answer is 2.

For a free cell, the longest plus sign centred there is limited by the **shortest of its four arms**. So compute, for each cell, how many free cells there are in a row **ending at it** (counting it) going from the left, from the right, from the top and from the bottom. The order of the plus sign centred at the cell is the smallest of these four numbers. Each of the four runs is a tiny DP: `run(j) = run(j - 1) + 1` for a free cell and 0 for a blocked one.

body.code:
best = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]            # best[i][j]: the smallest of the four runs so far
for i in range(n):
    run = 0
    for j in range(n):                         # from the left
        run = run + 1 if free[i][j] else 0
        best[i][j] = run
    run = 0
    for j in range(n - 1, -1, -1):             # from the right
        run = run + 1 if free[i][j] else 0
        best[i][j] = min(best[i][j], run)
# the same for the columns from the top and from the bottom, then the answer is the largest best[i][j]

body: Four passes over the grid, each of O(n^2) steps, give the answer in O(n^2) time and memory. Looking at the grid from all four sides, one side after another, and keeping a running minimum is a method that you can use for many questions about "the longest line through a cell".

statement: An `n` by `n` grid has `m` blocked cells; the other cells are free. A plus sign of order `k` is a free centre cell together with `k - 1` free cells in each of the four directions from it (all inside the grid). Print the largest order of a plus sign that fits, or 0 if there is no free cell.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the size of the square grid and the number of blocked cells.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `x` and `y`: a blocked cell (row `x`, column `y`, counted from 0).
constraints: The blocked cells are all different.

examples.note: A plus sign of order 2 fits: its centre has free neighbours in all four directions.

hints: For each free cell count the free cells in a row going from the left, from the right, from the top and from the bottom (including the cell).
The order of the plus sign centred at the cell is the smallest of the four numbers.
Take the largest order over all the cells.

explanation: For every cell the number of consecutive free cells ending at it is computed from the left, from the right, from the top and from the bottom; the order of the plus sign centred there is the smallest of the four, and the answer is the largest order over all cells.
